proof.text: The maps $c$ and $d$ are base changes of the etale maps $b$ and $a$, so are etale. Identify $B_{\Et}$, $(T_B)_{\Et}$, $U_{\Et}$ and $(Y_U)_{\Et}$ with the slices of $S_{\Et}$, $T_{\Et}$, $X_{\Et}$ and $Y_{\Et}$ at their indicated objects. The identification $Y_U\cong U\times_BT_B$ is given by the projections to $U$ and $T$: both sides classify pairs with the same image in $S$. Etale inverse image is restriction. In the following all inverse images denote the exact termwise functors on the unbounded derived categories stipulated in the statement. Write the canonical inverse-image comparisons as $\alpha_f:r_Uf^{-1}\cong f_U^{-1}r_B$, $\alpha_e:r_{Y_U}e^{-1}\cong e_U^{-1}r_{T_B}$, $\kappa:r_{Y_U}h^{-1}\cong h_U^{-1}r_U$ and $\ell:r_{T_B}g^{-1}\cong g_B^{-1}r_B$. Write $p_g:r_BRg_*\cong Rg_{B*}r_{T_B}$ and $p_h:r_URh_*\cong Rh_{U*}r_{Y_U}$ for the derived slice comparisons, with constant coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$. Thus $C_L^D=f_U^{-1}(p_{g,K})\circ\alpha_{f,Rg_*K}$ and $C_R^D=Rh_{U*}(\alpha_{e,K})\circ p_{h,e^{-1}K}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0EZR, lemma-base-change-local, displayed local identifications

proof.text:
Let $\theta:h^{-1}f^{-1}\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}$ and $\theta_U:h_U^{-1}f_U^{-1}\cong e_U^{-1}g_B^{-1}$ be the square comparisons. Their compatibility with the four inverse-image comparisons is the equation, for $N\in D(\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\Et}))$,
$$e_U^{-1}(\ell_N)\circ\alpha_{e,g^{-1}N}\circ r_{Y_U}(\theta_N)=\theta_{U,r_BN}\circ h_U^{-1}(\alpha_{f,N})\circ\kappa_{f^{-1}N}.$$
Here is why it is the canonical, rather than an arbitrary, square comparison: the direct-image composition identifications are induced by the projections of iterated fibre products and satisfy the associativity equation of [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-composition-coherence]. Their unit-compatible left-adjoint comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; applying [lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence] gives the displayed rebracketing equation at the sheaf level, with etale inverse image identified with restriction. The underlying composite scheme map in every path is $fa h_U=bf_Uh_U=bg_Be_U=ged$. Apply that equation termwise to a complex. Exactness of inverse images and restriction, together with cohomology comparison, shows that the termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms; clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] preserves composition when descending the equation to $D$. This proves the displayed equation for arbitrary unbounded $N$.

proof.text:
The counit compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], applied to $g$ localized at $B$, is the typed identity
$$r_{T_B}(\varepsilon_{g,K})=\varepsilon_{g_B,K_B}\circ g_B^{-1}(p_{g,K})\circ\ell_{Rg_*K}:r_{T_B}g^{-1}Rg_*K\longrightarrow K_B.$$
It applies with no boundedness hypothesis: that node is stated for every object of the unbounded derived category. The ringed-site module functors here are the abelian-sheaf functors because the ring and its pullbacks are the constant ring $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, with the canonical adjunction of Tag 07A7, remark-base-change

proof.text:
Put $A=f^{-1}Rg_*K$, $M=e^{-1}K$, and $t_K=e^{-1}(\varepsilon_{g,K})\circ\theta_{Rg_*K}:h^{-1}A\to M$. Define $t_{U,K_B}$ by the same formula for the local square. Step 2 at $N=Rg_*K$, followed by step 3, gives
$$\alpha_{e,K}\circ r_{Y_U}(t_K)=t_{U,K_B}\circ h_U^{-1}(C_L^D)\circ\kappa_A.$$
Indeed naturality of $\alpha_e$ first rewrites the left side as $e_U^{-1}(r_{T_B}\varepsilon_{g,K})\circ\alpha_{e,g^{-1}Rg_*K}\circ r_{Y_U}(\theta_{Rg_*K})$. Substitute step 3 and then step 2. Naturality of $\theta_U$ for $p_{g,K}:r_BRg_*K\to Rg_{B*}K_B$ moves $g_B^{-1}(p_{g,K})$ across $\theta_U$, leaving $h_U^{-1}(f_U^{-1}(p_{g,K})\circ\alpha_{f,Rg_*K})=h_U^{-1}(C_L^D)$.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, counit transpose formula, with the substitutions of steps 2 and 3

proof.text:
Use the derived slice counit compatibility for $h$ localized at $U$:
$$\varepsilon_{h_U,r_{Y_U}M}\circ h_U^{-1}(p_{h,M})\circ\kappa_{Rh_*M}=r_{Y_U}(\varepsilon_{h,M}).$$
For any arrow $v:A\to Rh_*M$ the transpose of $C_R^D\circ r_U(v)$ under $h_U^{-1}\dashv Rh_{U*}$ is therefore
$$\alpha_{e,K}\circ r_{Y_U}(\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ h^{-1}(v))\circ\kappa_A^{-1}.$$
To verify this formula, the definition of transpose first gives $\varepsilon_{h_U,M_U}\circ h_U^{-1}(Rh_{U*}(\alpha_{e,K})\circ p_{h,M}\circ r_U(v))$, where $M_U=e_U^{-1}K_B$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_{h_U}$ moves $\alpha_{e,K}$ to the front; the displayed counit identity replaces the next two factors, and naturality of $\kappa$ moves $v$ inside $r_{Y_U}h^{-1}$. This is precisely the asserted expression.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, derived adjunctions

proof.text: Take $v=\beta_K$. By the defining transpose formula in [sbc-def-base-change-map], $\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ h^{-1}(\beta_K)=t_K$. Thus step 5 and step 4 identify the transpose of $C_R^D\circ r_U(\beta_K)$ with $t_{U,K_B}\circ h_U^{-1}(C_L^D)$. This is also the transpose of $\beta_{U,K_B}\circ C_L^D$, by the local defining formula and naturality of the counit. The hom correspondence of the stipulated derived adjunction is a bijection, so the two arrows are equal. Every comparison used is natural in $K$, and $\beta$ is a natural transformation by its mate definition; hence this is an equality natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, equality tested after the adjunction bijection; Tag 0EZR, derived locality

proof.text:
Apply $H^q$ to the equality in step 6, for any $q\in\mathbf Z$. Restriction to $U$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]. Consequently the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies $H^q(r_U(-))$ with $r_UH^q(-)$; this applies to derived arrows as well, since the termwise natural comparison descends along $Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2). Its naturality identifies the restricted arrow, rather than only its source and target objects. Thus
$$H^q(C_R^D)\circ r_UH^q(\beta_K)=H^q(\beta_{U,K_B})\circ H^q(C_L^D)$$
under those comparisons. No positivity of $q$, boundedness of $K$, or qcqs assumption on a scheme morphism was used.

title: Derived base-change arrow under etale localization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes, with the Cartesian square $Y=X\times_ST$, $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $a:U\to X$ and $b:B\to S$ be etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $f_U:U\to B$ satisfy $fa=bf_U$. Put $T_B=B\times_ST$, with projections $g_B:T_B\to B$ and $c:T_B\to T$, and $Y_U=U\times_XY$, with projections $h_U:Y_U\to U$ and $d:Y_U\to Y$. The canonical identification $Y_U\cong U\times_BT_B$ defines $e_U:Y_U\to T_B$, so $ce_U=ed$. Work on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], and write $r_Z$ for restriction to an etale object $Z$. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Ab}(T_{\Et}))$ be an arbitrary unbounded complex of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and put $K_B=r_{T_B}K$. Use the exact etale inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and the unbounded derived direct images and canonical derived adjunctions of [sbc-def-base-change-map], specialized to constant coefficients $\mathbf Z$ (abelian sheaves). Write $\beta_K:f^{-1}Rg_*K\to Rh_*e^{-1}K$ for its counit-transpose base-change morphism, and $\beta_{U,K_B}$ for the corresponding morphism of $(f_U,g_B,h_U,e_U)$. Under the canonical comparisons
$$C_L^D:r_Uf^{-1}Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}f_U^{-1}r_BRg_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}f_U^{-1}Rg_{B*}K_B,$$
$$C_R^D:r_URh_*e^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{U*}r_{Y_U}e^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{U*}e_U^{-1}K_B,$$
induced by termwise inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], with etale inverse image identified with restriction [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], and the derived slice-localization comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], one has
$$C_R^D\circ r_U(\beta_K)=\beta_{U,K_B}\circ C_L^D.$$
This identity is natural in $K$. For every integer $q$, the exact-restriction/cohomology comparisons identify $r_UH^q(\beta_K)$ with $H^q(\beta_{U,K_B})$ under $H^q(C_L^D)$ and $H^q(C_R^D)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology].
